correctness.rationale: Under GRH for every Dirichlet L-function, the claimed envelope and count follow with the stated normalization. The product jump at p is Z(p)/p, so 1+sum_{p<=X} W(p)=Z(X). For p>X>=k every tail prime is coprime to k, and character orthogonality with weight 1/phi(k) cancels the principal character. The uniform nonprincipal bound in Thakur's equation (2) survives the average without a modulus-size multiplier. At X=k^(2+delta) the normalized error is O(log k/k^(delta/2)), and the subtracted product tends to 2+delta after division by e^gamma log k. The eligible prime r contributes at least 1/c-o(1) on the normalized scale: use Mertens with an arbitrary fixed relative tolerance and monotonicity of log u/u for large u, treat the finitely many small primes by their fixed positive weights, and use log phi(k)~log k. Taking delta to zero after the liminf yields 1/c-2. The primes represent different classes; PNT and omega(k)=O(log k)=o(phi(k)/log k) give the lower count, then c increases to 1/2. Thakur's nonnegative-class bound supplies the upper bound on strict positives.
residual_risks: All limits are conditional on Dirichlet GRH. The number 1/2 is a lower bound, not an exact asymptotic or an optimality statement.

value.rationale: The cited upper estimate says most signs are negative but leaves the scale of the exceptional positive set undetermined. The lower envelope identifies a uniform family of positive classes for composite as well as prime moduli and establishes that the positive exceptional set attains the scale of the upper bound. This answers a structural question about the signs without claiming a limiting count constant.
